rationale: P identifies braking behavior when braking is required, which must be characterised to evaluate whether required maneuvers are omitted. SG-1 and FR-7 establish braking itself as the relevant system behavior, while H-1 supports the collision-avoidance context and pedestrian scenario. P does not extend to sensing, computation, communication, fault mitigation, or their timing constraints merely because they influence braking.
determining_elements: “Vehicle braking behavior” is directly supported by SG-1’s prohibition of omitted required maneuvers and FR-7’s requirement to perform collision-avoidance braking.
“Situations where a braking maneuver is required to avoid a collision with an obstacle or road user” matches the hazardous event described in H-1.
The scope includes H-1’s straight-ahead driving scenario with a pedestrian crossing 20 m ahead.
The statement and scope remain focused on required braking rather than incorporating supporting mechanisms or unrelated response behavior.
